predeclaration_note: This file records the protocol that is executed verbatim by run_xval.py. It was frozen after the first exploratory pass whose only purpose was to check that the harness ran; that pass is what exposed the clip-floor failure and therefore added the ours_old_default arm and the clip=False/publication of the omega_min defect. The acceptance threshold (15%) is the owner criterion and the beta ladder {0.2,0.5,2,10,25,50}, the tolerance (1e-8 relative), the arms and the KPIs were NOT adjusted after inspecting the KPI values of the reported runs.
decision: Does TensorLBM's dynamic Aitken under-relaxation, run as the interface fixed point of a displacement-based strong-coupling sub-iteration, reproduce joconnor22/LIFE's displacement-Aitken under-relaxation fixed point within the owner 15% criterion -- on the converged interface solution, on the recovered relaxation factor, and on the sub-iteration cost -- and which convention knobs carry any difference?

reference.provenance: oss_solutions row 258, feature_slug NEW:LBM-FSI-BLOCK-GS-AITKEN, tag displacement-aitken-underrelaxation-fixed-point (frozen method digest, zero manual copying)
reference.frozen_method: do { U0 = 2.5 U_n - 2 U_{n-1} + 0.5 U_{n-2}; interpolate; FEM full re-solve (Newton-Raphson TOL=1e-10 MAXIT=20); residual } while (res > 1e-8 and it < 20). Aitken for k >= 2: relax = -relax * (r_{k-1}.(r_k - r_{k-1})) / |r_k - r_{k-1}|^2; U = U_{k-1} + relax*(U - U_{k-1}). Residual normalised by ref_L*sqrt(DOF). IBM force spread once after convergence.
reference.implementation: xval/aitken_underrelaxation_life/reference.py::life_fixed_point_step (independent code path, displacement interface variable, no clipping, order-2 predictor)

alternatives.ours_old_default: AitkenRelaxation(omega0=0.5) as shipped before this mission: clip floor omega_min = 0.05, ceiling 1.0, acceleration interface, no predictor, absolute residual tolerance
alternatives.ours_new_default: identical but with the corrected clip floor omega_min = 1e-4 (this mission's fix)
alternatives.ours_noclip: AitkenRelaxation(omega0=0.5, clip=False): raw Aitken, isolates the clipping effect from the predictor effect
alternatives.ours_life_conv: AitkenRelaxation(omega0=1.0, clip=False) + predictor='quadratic' + relative residual tolerance 1e-8: TensorLBM driver driven with LIFE's conventions
alternatives.none_control: plain fixed point omega = 1 (negative control: expected to diverge for beta_eff > 1)
alternatives.oracle_constant: constant omega = 1/(1+beta_eff) (oracle upper bound on achievable iteration count)

hypothesis.H1: Under aligned conventions (omega0 = 1, no clipping, order-2 predictor, relative 1e-8 residual) TensorLBM's Aitken fixed point is numerically identical to the LIFE transcription: max relative deviation of the applied relaxation factor on steps where both perform an Aitken update < 15%, and identical converged interface displacement.
hypothesis.H2: The pre-fix TensorLBM default (clip floor 0.05) deviates from the reference: the clipped floor omega_min = 0.05 gives |1 - omega_min (1+beta_eff)| > 1 for beta_eff > 39, hence non-convergence, and costs >15% more sub-iterations for beta_eff in (19, 39).
hypothesis.falsifier: H1 is falsified if any aligned arm shows >15% deviation in the recovered factor, >15% deviation in the converged interface displacement, or a different converged/no-converged verdict; H2 is falsified if the pre-fix default matches the reference within 15% at beta_eff = 50.

metrics.K3_iters_mean: mean sub-iterations per time step to the declared tolerance
metrics.K5_converged: every time step reached the tolerance inside max_iter
metrics.K6_recurrence_identity_pct: max relative deviation of the applied factor when TensorLBM's AitkenRelaxation and the LIFE secant formula are fed the same residual sequence (3 magnitudes, 12 residuals)

references_used.REF-D: monolithic Newmark, one solve per step with the total mass m_s + m_a (exact solution of the discrete coupled system)
references_used.REF-C: closed form of (m_s+m_a) d'' + c d' + k d = F0 sin(Omega t), rest initial conditions, under-damped
references_used.REF-W: analytic Aitken optimum omega* = 1/(1+beta_eff) (Irwin & Kesavan 2005; Kuettler & Wall 2008)

unit_of_analysis: one arm x one added-mass ratio; KPIs are scalars over a 3-period time-accurate run

predeclared_thresholds.pass_rule: K1, K2, K4 and K6 must be < 15% for the aligned arms (ours_life_conv vs life_ref); K5 must be true
predeclared_thresholds.iteration_cost_rule: a K3 difference between ours_life_conv and life_ref larger than 15% must be attributed to a listed convention difference (predictor, start factor, tolerance normalisation, clipping) or reported as an implementation defect; K3 is diagnostic, not an accuracy gate
predeclared_thresholds.physical_accuracy_rule: K2 < 3% is reported explicitly against the owner's stricter 3% question
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: non-finite interface state or |d| > 1e6 * (F0/k) is a failure, reported as measured, never tuned away

variables_changed: relaxation convention (clip floor, clip on/off, omega0, predictor, residual normalisation)
time resolution (100, 200, 400 steps per coupled period)
variables_controlled: F0 = 1 N sine at the coupled natural frequency
residual tolerance 1e-8 relative to ref_L = 1 m
max_iter = 200 for every arm (LIFE's own MAXIT = 20 is reported as satisfied, 3 iterations used)
float64 CPU numpy, single thread, deterministic (no random input; the only RNG use is the fixed-seed recurrence probe, seed 20261113)
confounders: interface variable (displacement in LIFE vs acceleration in tensorlbm.fsi_partitioned) -- the scalar Aitken secant is invariant under a constant scaling of the residual, verified in the recurrence probe

residual normalisation (LIFE: |delta d|/(ref_L sqrt(DOF)); TensorLBM: unnormalised |r_a|) -- converted by the Newmark identity delta d = beta_N dt^2 delta a so both arms stop at the same physical increment

very light damping (zeta = 0.003) and resonant drive make per-step tolerance errors accumulate secularly; this inflates K1 for arms that ride the tolerance instead of converging to machine precision and is reported, not hidden
repetition_rationale: the computation is fully deterministic (no stochastic input, single thread), so one run per cell is sufficient; the discriminating evidence comes from the beta ladder (6 levels) and two sensitivity sweeps rather than from repetitions
stopping_rule: each arm runs exactly 3 coupled periods (600 steps at 200 steps/period); no arm is extended or truncated after inspecting its KPI
analysis: per-cell scalars are written to out/summary.csv and out/results.json by run_xval.py; deviations are relative (percent) against the reference of the same cell; no outlier removal, no smoothing; failed cells are kept and flagged
interpretation_limits: 1-DOF interface: the scalar Aitken secant is exact for a linear scalar map, so iteration counts here are a lower bound compared with multi-DOF FEM structures where the scalar factor cannot annihilate a multi-mode error
no LBM fluid: the fluid operator is the exact added-mass law F = F_ext - m_a a (linear, incompressible column); IBM spreading/interpolation error is out of scope

the OSS code could not be executed (no network in the mission sandbox); the reference is the frozen method digest plus an independent transcription, so 'agreement' verifies the algorithm, not the OSS binary
